description: Being declared unclean and requiring ritual cleansing; confinement for a set period; eating from broken plates; sleeping on the bare floor; shaving the head; wearing prescribed white or dark robes. One account describes 28 days of seclusion without leaving the compound, followed by a further two or five months of mourning depending on local custom.
energy_note: Twenty-eight days indoors, and her head shaved.

description: Widow inheritance - marrying a late husband's brother or relative, voluntarily or compulsorily - persists in some communities. In-laws, clans and village heads may demand the late husband's property and sell some off ostensibly to fund the burial.
energy_note: Widowed on Tuesday, and the property is being valued by Friday.

aspect: It is enforced by women as well as men
description: The husband's family, kinsmen, and local women's associations all enforce these practices - in some communities the Umuada, the daughters of the lineage. Which removes the assumption that solidarity is automatic.
energy_note: The women of the family, enforcing it on the widow.

aspect: Compliance is bought with fear of the alternative
description: A Delta State study found submission stems from fear of social exclusion, ostracisation, expulsion from the late husband's house or village, and disinheritance of the widow and her children.
energy_note: Agreeing to it, because refusing costs the children their home.

aspect: Widowers are not subject to any of it
description: The asymmetry is total and is the clearest available demonstration that the practices are about property and control rather than mourning.
energy_note: He buries her and goes to work on Monday.

aspect: The law, and the one case people cite
description: VAPP 2015 prescribes up to two years or a N500,000 fine. Cross River's Prohibition of Domestic Violence and Maltreatment of Widows Law No. 6 of 2005 provides a N20,000 fine and 3 years. In Ojukwu v Ojukwu, where relatives tried to evict a widow and her children citing male-only customary inheritance, the court held a widow cannot be treated as a stranger in her own home.
energy_note: Illegal, in several statutes, and widely practised.

description: In 2026 the Minister of Women Affairs condemned disinheritance, property grabbing, forced confinement and degrading mourning rites as criminal, noting more than two million widows in Nigeria carry caregiving and breadwinning responsibilities under difficult economic conditions.
energy_note: Two million women, and a ministerial statement.

Alongside the case law, documented practice includes twenty-eight days of seclusion without leaving the compound, followed by a further two or five months of mourning depending on local custom, with the head shaved and prescribed robes worn throughout.
energy_note: A judgment in her favour, and twenty-eight days indoors regardless.

aspect: The rites end and the position does not
description: After the seclusion, the mourning and the cleansing, she returns to a household where the property question was settled during the months she was not permitted to leave the compound. The rites are not only humiliation; they are the interval during which the decisions get made.
energy_note: Secluded for the exact period in which it was decided.
